note: The user's own photographs and video of a real shopping trip, provided explicitly as the verification set for this pipeline. Not redistributable: the files stay in .cache/ and are not committed. This manifest records what they are so the measurements below can be read without them.
source: photographed by the user, supplied directly for this purpose
licence: not redistributable; used with the owner's explicit permission
capture: iPhone, HEIC stills at 5712x4284 and one HEVC video at 1080x1920 portrait, 30fps
why_this_corpus: Every other corpus here is a substitute. The shelf corpus is Indian retail shelves, the cart corpus is openly-licensed haul photographs mostly taken on tables, and RPC is products on a turntable. This is the actual thing: a phone held over a real trolley in a real shop, with the trolley's own wire mesh between the camera and the goods.

video.content: a scan session over the loaded trolley of IMG_0252

verified_complete: Checked against ~/Downloads/kart-images:video on 2026-08-22: the folder holds exactly ten HEIC stills, IMG_0244 to IMG_0252 and IMG_0254, and one MOV. There is no unused material, so the corpus is not a subset of what was supplied and cannot be grown from what is here.
conversion_is_lossless: The cached JPEGs are the full 5712 by 4284 with a luma quantization table starting at 1, and are nearly twice the size of the HEIC originals. The conversion was done at maximum quality, so no measurement in KART.md is reading a degraded copy. Worth recording because the failures that remain are small-text and small-object ones, where a lossy re-encode would have been a plausible cause and is now ruled out.
